
RESEARCH
List the research tools available during Example Mapping

WHEN TO USE
  Use during the specifying phase to see which research tools are configured. For AST code search, use the `fspec astgrep` command instead.

USAGE
  fspec research [--tool=<name>] [--work-unit=<workUnitId>]

OPTIONS
  --tool <name>
    Research tool to select (perplexity, jira, confluence, stakeholder). Omit to list the tools. Running a tool is not ported yet.
  --work-unit <workUnitId>
    Work unit context for the tool

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Check which research tools are configured
    Example: fspec research
    Lists each bundled tool with ✓ (configured) or ✗ and the environment variable it needs


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  During Example Mapping, identify a question that needs research. Add question: fspec add-question AUTH-001 "@human: Support OAuth?". Ask the stakeholder or check the tools listed by fspec research. Answer question: fspec answer-question AUTH-001 0 --answer "Yes" --add-to rule. Generate scenarios: fspec generate-scenarios AUTH-001

EXAMPLES
  1. List all available research tools
  $ fspec research
  Available Research Tools:

  ✗ perplexity
    Perplexity AI research tool for web search and AI-powered answers
    Usage: fspec research --tool=perplexity <args>
    Config: export PERPLEXITY_API_KEY="..."

  2. Select a tool (execution is not ported yet)
  $ fspec research --tool=stakeholder --work-unit=AUTH-001
  Research tool execution is not yet ported to the Rust binary (tool 'stakeholder'); use the listing mode (omit --tool) for now

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: Research tool not found: xyz
    Fix: Run fspec research to list the available tools

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec add-question
  fspec answer-question
  fspec add-attachment
  fspec generate-scenarios

NOTES
  • Bundled tools: perplexity, jira, confluence, stakeholder
  • Each tool shows the environment variable that configures it
  • Running a research tool is not ported to the Rust CLI yet
  • Attachments are saved to spec/attachments/<workUnitId>/
  • For AST code search and refactoring, use the `fspec astgrep` command
